newsitem.title: USA: Workplace safety citations up last year, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: Workplace safety citations up last year, U.S. says.

text.p: The number of citations issued last year for very serious workplace safety violations increased by more than 30 percent, federal regulators said Friday.

The Labor Department's Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) said it issued 165 citations for so-called significant and egregious enforcement cases in the government's fiscal year ended Sept. 30, compared with 125 in the previous year.
"When it comes to workplace safety and health, we will continue to collaborate with responsible business," said Labor Secretary Robert Reich. "But OSHA also must continue to be the cop on the beat."
OSHA defines significant cases as those where it has proposed penalties of more than $100,000 and egregious cases as those where multiple willful violations warrant instance-by-instance penalties.
